facts.text: Garyville was founded in 1906 as a company town by the Godchaux Sugar Refinery, which remains a major employer and landmark in the area.
Garyville once led the world in lumber production and attracted many Italian and Sicilian immigrants, becoming one of the largest Sicilian communities outside New Orleans and Baton Rouge.
The Garyville Historic District features the Timbermill Museum, the historic Gary State Bank, and the long‑standing Garyville General Store.
San Francisco Plantation, located in Garyville, is considered the most opulent plantation house in North America.
Garyville is part of the New Orleans–Metairie–Kenner metropolitan statistical area, linking it to the larger Gulf Coast region.
Geographically, Garyville sits at 30°3′26″N 90°37′7″W, placing it just north of the Mississippi River.
